audit.whatIsWrong: Lane difficulty is framed around a Tongue Lash 'stun' that is always available. Tongue Lash (Q) does not stun on its own — it stuns only when the target already carries 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste (P), which he must build with three separate damaging hits.
audit.why: This is the single decision that governs every trade: the danger is not the tongue, it is the third hit. Rumble players who treat Q as an on-demand stun give up free trades; players who treat it as harmless eat the stun.
audit.corrected: Difficulty is real but conditional — count his stacks. At 0-1 stacks Rumble can trade freely at Flamespitter range; at 2 stacks the next contact stuns and the lane flips.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Riot Data Dragon description of An Acquired Taste and Tongue Lash)

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike list never mentions Abyssal Dive (W), his only gap-closer and his only knockup, and the level-6 entry treats Devour as a free reset when it needs 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste first.
audit.why: Rumble's whole safety model is standing at Flamespitter/Electro Harpoon range. The ability that breaks that range is Abyssal Dive at 1000 range on a 21s rank-1 cooldown, and that cooldown is the spike window worth playing around.
audit.corrected: Level 6 spike is Abyssal Dive plus Devour together, and both are gated: Devour needs 3 An Acquired Taste stacks, Abyssal Dive is down 21s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Abyssal Dive cooldown 21/20/19/18/17, range 1000-1200; Devour cost/stack gate)

audit.whatIsWrong: Two interaction claims are wrong or unsupported: (a) 'Tongue Lash stun' is asserted unconditionally throughout both layers; (b) 'Use double Electro-Harpoon to cancel his Devour animation' asserts an interrupt that Riot's text does not support.
audit.why: Point 4 is the user's key point and the audit's most-important item. Electro Harpoon has no interrupt or cast-stop property in its description — it deals damage, slows, and shreds MR. Asserting a cancel a player will trust is the exact failure mode the brief forbids.
audit.corrected: Real interactions worth stating: Electro Harpoon shreds MR before Flamespitter's burn ticks; Thick Skin (E) turns stored damage into a shield on a 3s cooldown, so burst that outpaces the store beats chip that feeds it; Abyssal Dive's knockup is his only hard engage.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (Electro Harpoon description: damage, slow, MR reduction — no interrupt)

audit.why: Grievous Wounds is already core in the itemization block, which is right — Tongue Lash heals on champion hit and Thick Skin heals out of combat.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing records that Rumble's Scrap Shield is only a shield plus a move-speed burst.
audit.why: The derived flags in the kit library tag Scrap Shield with 'knockup' and 'terrain', and _missing-interactions.json repeats that as 'both sides carry displacement'. Riot's own description contains neither. I did not propagate it.
audit.corrected: No edit made — flagged so the bad flag is not written into any matchup.

notes: Two data defects worth the user's attention. (1) The derived flags in champ-data/_kits/rumble.json tag Scrap Shield (W) with 'knockup' and 'terrain'; Riot's description is only a shield plus a move-speed burst. _missing-interactions.json inherits this and emits 'Both sides carry displacement (Scrap Shield (W) vs Abyssal Dive (W))' for this matchup — false, and it recurs across the whole Rumble set. I did not propagate it. (2) The packet suspectName flagging 'Save Equalizer' in wants.you[2] is a false positive; 'Equalizer' is the correct short form of The Equalizer. The genuine error in this matchup was the unconditional 'Tongue Lash stun', which the near-miss scanner cannot see because the name is spelled correctly.
